correctness.rationale: The exact common-core lemma supplies one-per-window-edge binary selection difference. Step decomposition and integration through piecewise-linear ranking chambers establish the global bound; the explicit even/odd permutation has an exactly counted, unit-jump middle-rank tag sequence on all window edges. Endpoint extension and the strict shorter-path edge-count bound give attainment and the minimum saturation length. The accompanying checker reproduced all exact arithmetic identities for radii 1 through 30 and all trimming levels, exhaustively tested small ranking chambers and performed 1,500 supplementary random two-input checks.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a natural, complete exact stability tradeoff between moving averages and running medians for all discrete central trimming fractions and all radii. The common-core cancellation is not implied by averaging individual rank stability estimates. The sharp minimum path length identifies the first record length at which full perturbation sensitivity is possible, a meaningful finite-size boundary for robust sliding smoothers.
